fields.title: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
fields.bodyHtml:
ADHD (attention deficit hyperactivity disorder): approaches to treatment in Israel

ADHD is a common neurodevelopmental condition characterised by difficulties with attention, impulsiveness and, in some cases, hyperactivity. Israeli medical centres use a comprehensive approach to treating ADHD, combining medication, psychotherapy and educational and support programmes.

Diagnosis of ADHD

  1. Psychological testing: Assessment of cognitive function, attention, concentration and patterns of behaviour.
  2. Medical examination: Ruling out physical conditions that can produce symptoms resembling ADHD.
  3. Questionnaires and rating scales: Used to gather information from parents, teachers and the child about their behaviour in different settings.
  4. Neurological examination: Assessment of neurological status to identify possible abnormalities.

Treatments for ADHD in Israel

  1. Medication:
    • Stimulants (methylphenidate, for example): Improve attention and reduce impulsiveness and hyperactivity.
    • Non-stimulants (atomoxetine, for example): May be used where stimulants are unsuitable or cause side effects.
  2. Psychotherapy:
    • Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT): Helps develop skills of self-control, managing attention and planning.
    • Behavioural therapy: Aimed at improving behaviour at home and at school.
  3. Family counselling and training: Support for parents in bringing up and communicating with a child who has ADHD.
  4. Educational programmes and support sessions: Adapting the learning process to the child's needs and working on improving study skills.
  5. Diet and lifestyle changes: In some cases adjusting the diet and introducing regular exercise can improve the symptoms of ADHD.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Comprehensive assessment and treatment of the child by a team of specialists including psychologists, psychiatrists, neurologists and educators.
  • An individualised treatment plan: The development of a personal treatment and support strategy for each child and family.
  • Access to the newest treatments: The use of advanced medicines and therapeutic techniques.
  • Support and education for the family: Involving parents in the treatment process and giving them the tools to understand and support their child better.

Treatment of ADHD in Israel aims not only to improve the symptoms of the condition but also to integrate the child fully into social and school life, helping them realise their potential to the full.

fields.title: Synovial sarcoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Synovial sarcoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Synovial sarcoma is a rare type of malignant tumour that most often develops near the joints, particularly in the area of the knees, arms and legs. In Israel, patients have access to advanced treatments including surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy, as well as the newest approaches in targeted and immune therapy.

Diagnosis of synovial sarcoma:

  1. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Used to assess the size, position and extent of the tumour and how it relates to the surrounding tissues.
  2. Computed tomography (CT):
    Helps establish whether there are metastases, particularly in the lungs.
  3. Biopsy:
    The key method for obtaining an accurate diagnosis. It may be carried out as an open biopsy or with a fine needle under CT or ultrasound guidance.
  4. PET-CT:
    Effective in assessing the metabolic activity of the tumour and detecting distant metastases.
  5. Laboratory tests:
    These include blood tests to assess general health and the functioning of the organs.

Treatments for synovial sarcoma:

  1. Surgery:
    • Wide local resection: Removal of the tumour together with a margin of healthy tissue around it to minimise the risk of recurrence.
    • Lymphadenectomy: Where metastases in the lymph nodes are suspected.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • May be given before or after the operation to destroy any remaining cancer cells or to shrink the tumour before surgery.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used as neoadjuvant (before surgery) or adjuvant (after surgery) therapy to destroy cancer cells and reduce the risk of the cancer spreading.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • Targeted medicines: Directed at specific molecular targets involved in the growth and survival of cancer cells.
    • Immunotherapy: Medicines that activate the immune system to fight the cancer.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Oncologists, surgeons, radiologists and other specialists work together to develop an individual treatment plan.
  • Advanced medical equipment and treatments: The use of the newest technology and treatment protocols.
  • Individual treatment: Every treatment plan is adapted to the needs and circumstances of the patient, including their psychological state.

Treatment of synovial sarcoma in Israel aims to achieve the best possible results, minimise side effects and improve patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)
fields.bodyHtml:
A continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system is a modern device designed to measure the level of glucose in the blood continuously and in real time. CGM is used primarily in the management of diabetes and allows patients to control their sugar levels more precisely, preventing sharp rises and falls.

How does a CGM system work?

A CGM system has several main components:

  1. The sensor — a small detector placed under the skin, which measures the level of glucose in the interstitial fluid every few minutes.
  2. The transmitter — attaches to the sensor and sends the data to a reader (a smartphone, an insulin pump or a special monitor).
  3. The receiver or app — the device that displays the data, allowing the patient to follow their sugar levels.

The system measures glucose every 1–5 minutes and transmits the data in real time, giving the user a graph of their sugar levels and warnings when readings are too high or too low.

Advantages of using CGM

  1. Continuous monitoring: allows changes in sugar levels to be tracked around the clock, including during sleep and physical activity.
  2. Warnings: the system alerts the user to low or high blood sugar before it occurs.
  3. Better treatment: using the CGM data, the doctor can adjust the insulin dose or choose more suitable therapy.
  4. Tracking trends: the device shows how various factors (food, exercise, stress) affect sugar levels.
  5. Convenience: removes the need for frequent sugar measurements with a glucose meter and finger pricks.

When CGM is used

  • Type 1 diabetes (particularly in children and adolescents).
  • Type 2 diabetes with frequent episodes of low blood sugar.
  • Frequent episodes of low or high blood sugar.
  • Poorly controlled diabetes (unstable sugar levels).
  • Use of an insulin pump.
  • Pregnancy in women with diabetes.

How is CGM fitted?

  1. Fitting the sensor: the sensor is attached to the skin on the abdomen, upper arm or thigh. Fitting is painless and takes only a few minutes.
  2. Connecting the transmitter: the transmitter is connected to the sensor and begins sending data.
  3. Syncing with a device: the glucose data is sent to the receiver or smartphone by Bluetooth or another wireless connection.

Common CGM systems

There are several leading manufacturers of CGM systems on the market:

  • Dexcom G6: an accurate and convenient system that works without finger pricks.
  • FreeStyle Libre: a compact device that is simple to fit and scans the sugar level.
  • Medtronic Guardian Connect: integrates with Medtronic insulin pumps.

Frequently asked questions

  1. Is CGM suitable for everyone with diabetes?
    CGM is suitable for most patients, but whether the device is needed is decided by the doctor, based on the type of diabetes, how often low blood sugar occurs and other factors.
  2. How does CGM differ from a glucose meter?
    A glucose meter shows the sugar level only at the moment of measurement, whereas CGM tracks it 24/7, showing trends and warning of risks.
  3. Is fitting the sensor painful?
    No, fitting the sensor is practically painless and takes only a few minutes.
  4. Can CGM be worn during sport?
    Yes, most CGM devices are water- and dust-resistant, so they can be used during physical activity.
  5. How much does a CGM system cost?
    The cost depends on the model, the country and the healthcare system. Some systems may be partly covered by insurance.

Conclusion

Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is an innovative technology that makes managing diabetes more convenient and more effective. Thanks to constant monitoring of sugar levels, patients can avoid sharp swings, improve their quality of life and reduce the risk of complications. If you would like to start using CGM, consult an endocrinologist to find the right device for you.

fields.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)
fields.bodyHtml:
Systemic lupus erythematosus: modern treatment in Israel

Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissues and organs. This can lead to inflammation and damage in various systems of the body, including the skin, joints, kidneys, heart and lungs. SLE can produce a wide variety of symptoms, which makes it difficult to diagnose and treat. Israeli clinics offer advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment aimed at improving patients' quality of life and preventing complications.

Diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus in Israel

Diagnosis of SLE in Israel involves a comprehensive approach based on modern technology and the deep knowledge of its specialists. The main methods of diagnosis include:

  • Clinical examination and history: a detailed study of the patient's symptoms and medical history.
  • Laboratory tests: blood and urine tests to identify the characteristic signs of inflammation and autoimmune reactions.
  • Immunological tests: detection of specific antibodies such as antinuclear antibodies (ANA), anti-dsDNA and other markers indicating SLE.
  • Biopsy: examination of tissue samples to assess the extent of damage to the organs.
  • Imaging: ultrasound, computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess the state of the internal organs.

Treatments for systemic lupus erythematosus in Israel

Treatment of SLE in Israel aims to reduce inflammation, control symptoms and prevent damage to the organs. The main treatments include:

  • Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs):
    • Naproxen and ibuprofen: reduce inflammation and address symptoms in the joints; often used as short-term therapy.
  • Steroid ointments: help with the skin rashes caused by lupus.
  • Antimalarial medicines:
    • Hydroxychloroquine: used on its own or in combination with topical steroids for skin rashes; it helps with fatigue and joint pain, lowers cholesterol levels and helps control kidney disease.
  • Steroid tablets:
    • Prednisolone: used as short-term therapy for complications such as pleurisy or pericarditis, and as long-term therapy for other problems including inflammation of the kidneys or serious disorders of the blood-forming system.
  • Disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs):
    • Azathioprine, ciclosporin, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, mycophenolate: used to suppress the overactive immune system and control raised blood pressure; they help prevent kidney problems and are often used together with steroid tablets so that the steroid dose can be reduced.
  • Biological therapies:
    • Rituximab and belimumab: block or reduce the activity of B cells — the white blood cells that produce the harmful autoantibodies — and are used in lupus where conventional DMARDs do not help.
  • Steroid injections: used for urgent treatment during a lupus flare-up, and can be injected into the scalp where there is hair loss.

Advantages of treating systemic lupus erythematosus in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists: doctors with many years of experience in treating SLE and other autoimmune conditions.
  2. Modern technology and equipment: the use of advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment.
  3. A comprehensive approach: individually designed treatment programmes that take account of every feature of the patient's case.
  4. Innovative methods: access to the latest advances in biological therapy and immunotherapy.
  5. Comfortable conditions: a high standard of service and support for patients at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of SLE in Israel aims to achieve lasting remission, improve patients' quality of life and minimise the risk of complications. Thanks to advanced methods and the high professionalism of its doctors, patients can expect the best results in the fight against this complex disease.
